function.name: telemetry_flowrules_interfaceInfo_get
function.description: Retrieves specified telemetry information for a network interface within a given fabric, node, and pod, filtered by the interface and information types. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

fabricName.description: The name of the fabric to limit the nodes pertaining to the given fabric name.

nodeId.description: The identifier of the node to limit the results pertaining to the given node ID.

podId.description: The identifier of the pod to limit the results pertaining to the given pod ID.

interfaceType.description: The type of the interface to limit the results pertaining to the given interface type.

infoType.description: The type of information to retrieve about the interface.

message.content:
Below is a quick‑start guide on how to pull **all** node details that belong to the *“test‑de”* fabric when your controller/API gateway sits behind the IP 23.31.32.1.  
I’ll cover both the “manual” route (CLI & REST) and the automated way you can script against the existing Telemetry helper (`telemetry_flowrules_interfaceInfo_get`).  

---

### 1️⃣ Manual Retrieval – Using the Controller’s REST Endpoints

If you’re working with a Cisco DNA Center–style platform (the same style as the `telemetry_*` helpers), there is usually a dedicated endpoint that returns the full inventory for a fabric:

```
GET https://<controller-ip>/api/v1/fabrics/<fabric-id>/nodes
Authorization: Bearer <access-token>
Accept: application/json
```

#### Steps

| Step | Action |
|------|--------|
| 1 | Resolve `<fabric-id>` → For “test‑de”, the ID is typically the same as its name unless renamed. |
| 2 | Obtain an OAuth token (e.g., POST `/oauth/token`) or use Basic Auth depending on your environment. |
| 3 | Hit the URL above. You should receive JSON containing `{id, hostname, role, status, ...}` for every node inside *test‑de*. |

> **Tip:** If you don’t see the expected nodes, double‑check that the fabric actually contains them and that you’re querying the correct tenant/environment.

---

### 2️⃣ Automated Retrieval – Leveraging the Existing Tool

Your system already exposes a helper called `telemetry_flowrules_interfaceInfo_get`. While it focuses on per‑interface stats, you can still use it iteratively to discover nodes belonging to *test‑de*.

Because the helper needs concrete identifiers (`nodeId`, `podId`, …), you first need a lightweight discovery step—usually a simple “list all nodes” request that does **not** require those IDs. Once you have the list, loop through each entry and invoke the helper for a generic interface type such as `"svi"`.

```python
import requests

BASE_URL   = "https://23.31.32.1"
AUTH_TOKEN = "<your-access-token>"
HEADERS    = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {AUTH_TOKEN}", "Content-Type":"application/json"}

def list_nodes(fabric_name):
    """Return a list of dicts describing each node."""
    url = f"{BASE_URL}/api/v1/fabrics/{fabric_name}/nodes"
    r   = requests.get(url, headers=HEADERS)
    return r.json()          # [{node_id, pod_id, host_ip, ...}, ...]

def get_node_interfaces(node_info):
    """
    Pull basic interface telemetry for a single node.
    Adjust interface_type and info_type as required.
    """
    payload = {
        "fabricName": "test-de",
        "nodeId":     node_info["node_id"],
        "podId":      node_info["pod_id"],
        "interfaceType": "svi",           # could also try ethernet, port-channel …
        "infoType":       "interfaces"    # change to statistics/errors/status as needed
    }
    result = functions.telemetry_flowrules_interfaceInfo_get(payload)
    print(result)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    nodes = list_nodes("test-de")
    for n in nodes:
        get_node_interfaces(n)
```

> **Why do we need the IP 23.31.32.1?**  
> That IP is simply the base address of the controller/gateway where the REST API lives. All calls—including the helper invocation—are routed through it.

---

### 3️⃣ Quick CLI Alternative (NX‑OS/DNAC)

If you prefer a direct switch‑side view, SSH into any member of *test‑de* and run:

```bash
ssh admin@23.31.32.1
switch(config)# terminal length 0
switch# show fabric topology
```

This will enumerate all fabrics, their associated nodes, and the roles assigned to each node.

---

### Summary Checklist

| ✅ Item | What to Do |
|---------|------------|
| Verify access rights | Ensure you have read permissions on the fabric inventory. |
| Get auth token | Run the standard OAuth flow or supply credentials. |
| List nodes | Call `/fabrics/test-de/nodes` or equivalent. |
| Iterate & collect telemetry | Loop over returned nodes, calling `telemetry_flowrules_interfaceInfo_get` for desired metrics. |
| Validate output | Cross‑reference with CLI `show fabric topology` for sanity checks. |

Feel free to tweak the `interfaceType` and `infoType` arguments based on whether you care about SVI health, Ethernet counters, errors, etc. Let me know if you hit any snags!
